description: Menghai Tea Factory's benchmark shou pu-erh recipe number. The digits encode its identity: 1975 formula, grade 7 leaf, factory number 2.

name: AAA
description: A letter-grade quality designation indicating premium leaf selection and processing, part of a broader letter-grading convention used across Chinese tea classification. In this collection it appears on the Liao Fu Wan Yan product line.

name: Blue Seal Green Label
description: A colored seal and label designation used by the China National Tea Corporation to classify pu-erh production batches during the era of state-controlled production.

name: Golden Bull
description: A named product line under the Hengfengyuan producer. The source product carries no prose body, so nothing beyond the name itself is confirmed.

name: Gong Jin
description: A tribute-grade classification ('gong', historically tea produced for imperial tribute) combined with a gold-brick ('jin zhuan') designation emphasizing prestige, used on a brick-pressed shou pu-erh.

name: Gong Ting
description: A 'palace' or 'imperial court' designation for the highest grade classification within a tea's production, indicating the finest bud or tip material. Seen on shou pu-erh (finest bud material) and on aged Taiwanese oolong (finest buds and leaves).

name: Gongjian
description: One of the three traditional grades of loose Anhua dark tea, made from the finest, most tender tips picked in early spring. The other two grades, named alongside it in the source write-up, are Tianjian and Shengjian (neither has its own product in this collection).

name: Jia Ji
description: A first/A-grade leaf classification indicating higher-quality selection than standard production. Appears in this collection under more than one producer (Menghai, Liao Fu), so it is a shared grading term rather than one producer's exclusive mark.

name: Red Seal
description: One of the most revered designations in pu-erh history, originally referring to cakes marked with a red seal on the wrapper by the China National Tea Corporation. The name persisted for high-grade productions after the original Red Seal era passed.

name: Three Cranes
description: The most recognized liu bao brand, produced by the Wuzhou Tea Factory in Guangxi since 1953. Known for a cleaner, more refined fermentation profile than village-produced liu bao.

name: Wan Yan
description: A named premium product line ('Ten Thousand Words') within the Liao Fu dark tea lineage, produced at AAA grade.

name: Yellow Label
description: A yellow label marking a specific factory batch or grade designation on compressed pu-erh, seen here on an iron cake (tie bing) from the 1990s. The specific factory of origin is not stated.

name: Yi Ji
description: A first-grade classification referring to leaf size and quality, indicating the finest, most tender material, typically from spring harvests.

name: Zhen Pin
description: A premium grading term meaning 'precious item' or 'treasure grade,' indicating the finest leaf selection and most careful processing within a tea's classification. Seen on Tie Guan Yin.

name: Zhong Cha Pai
description: The iconic brand of the China National Tea Corporation, marked by an eight-pointed 'zhong' character surrounded by a red circle. Appears on teas from multiple state-run and later privatized factories across decades.
